title: Midnight is playing at the Daryl Roth Theatre now through November 8t...
transcript: Unfortunately, this musical very much lives up to its title and is indeed a mid night at the theater. This is a very bold and ambitious new musical that certainly has a lot to appreciate. It has maybe one of the most talented casts in New York singing and dancing their butts off. It's also quite stunning from its overall design to its lighting to its choreography and costumes. It is a visually beautiful show to watch. And if you are someone that goes to the theatre for those things, I do think you are going to love this show. But when you look beyond the spectacle of the show, that's when a lot of the structural issues really start to appear. This show is cramming nearly everything it possibly can into its almost three hour run time. And because of that, the show loses focus a bit. There are so many characters that it's really hard to feel invested in anyone's journey outside of our main couple. So much so that there are major character beats that I just wasn't feeling what the show clearly wanted me to feel because I wasn't invested in these side characters. And even that core central love story gets bogged down by a lot of additional elements that are at play. Both of the men have an additional female love interest, both of which they have zero sexual chemistry with. Like, one of them gets pregnant at one point and I was like, are you Sure it's his? And then you have the major twist in Act 2, which you've probably heard about by now, but I won't spoil here if you haven't. But there is a bit of a reset that happens, which makes it even harder to invest in the characters because it feels like we're starting from square one. And also contributes to this muddling of the central romance, which is supposedly what the show is all about. I really feel like Todrick Hall, as talented as he is, really bit off more than he could chew here, because not only is he starring in it, not only did he write the entire show book, music, and lyrics. But he also directed it, choreographed it, serves as lead producer. And while don't get me wrong, it is a marvel that he is able to do all of these things at the caliber that he is doing them, part of what makes great theater is collaboration, and bringing in other creatives with different POV I think, would have helped iron out some of these kinks and would have allowed Todrick to focus on honing one part of the show rather than trying to hone the entire show at one time, which is an impossible task for almost anyone. Now, a lot has been said recently about the show's depiction of black trauma, with many black audience members feeling uncomfortable with the way that it's depicted here. I don't really feel like It is my place to comment on any of that, Many incredible black creators already have. But I will say if you are someone that is triggered by depictions of slavery or black trauma, definitely read up on the plot of the show. Watch videos from black creators talking about their experiences with the show to figure out for yourself if this is something you will enjoy because there are a lot of sensitive topics discussed here. But just to close out this review, I understand why this show has been as divisive as it is. Midnight is a show that has a lot to enjoy, but it is also far from a perfect musical. And while it highlights a lot of what makes Todrick Hall such a great artist, it also, in my opinion, highlights a lot of his shortcomings as well.
